reply.thought: I need to verify that the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds in my system before proceeding with payouts.
The refunds I have on record match exactly the refunds reported by Alpha Co. No discrepancies found, so I can proceed to calculate each customer's net balance and record the payouts.

The net_balance tool returned an error indicating that customer '480' does not exist. This suggests that the order IDs and customer IDs may not align directly; I need to verify the correct customer associated with these order IDs before proceeding.
I have the orders and their customers. Now I need to compute each customer's net balance (order amounts minus refunds) using net_balance for each customer. I'll start with customer 'acme'.
I have the net balance for customer 'acme'. Next I need the net balance for customer 'birch'.
I have the net balance for customer 'birch'. Next I need the net balance for customer 'cobalt'.
All net balances have been retrieved. Now I will record the payouts for each customer.
The payout for customer 'acme' has been recorded successfully. Now I need to record the payout for customer 'birch'.

result.error: bad arguments: World.record_payout() got an unexpected keyword argument 'amount_ccents'. Did you mean 'amount_cents'?

reply.thought: I made a typo in the argument name; the correct field is 'amount_cents'. I will correct it and record the payout for customer 'birch'.
The payout for customer  'birch' has been recorded. Now I need to record the payout for customer  'cobalt'.
